detail.title: [Failing Test] ci-kubernetes-node-e2e-containerd-serial failing with rotating specs
detail.body:
### Which jobs are failing?

- `ci-kubernetes-node-e2e-containerd-serial` (prow job name resolved via TestGrid `table` endpoint `.query = kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-node-e2e-containerd-serial`)
  - TestGrid tab: https://testgrid.k8s.io/sig-node-containerd#ci-node-e2e-serial

### Which tests are failing?

Job-level failure — no individual test row has alerted in TestGrid. The alerting rows are only the harness rows:

- `ci-kubernetes-node-e2e-containerd-serial.Overall` (fail_count 3)
- `kubetest.Node Tests` (fail_count 3)

Per-build junit shows the underlying spec failure **rotates** — a different test fails each run, so no single spec hits the 3-consecutive alert threshold:

- Build `2100188711563038720` (2026-09-16): ubuntu host failed `[It] [sig-node] Summary API when querying /stats/summary under pressure [FeatureGate:KubeletPSI] should report Memory pressure in PSI metrics` — suite timeout (`[TIMEDOUT] A suite timeout occurred ... at summary_test.go:406`). cos host: 0 failures.
- Build `2100158262149124096`: cos host failed `[It] [sig-node] GarbageCollect Garbage Collection Test: Many Restarting Containers Should eventually garbage collect containers when we exceed the number of dead containers per container`. ubuntu host: 0 failures.
- Build `2100128061046394880`: ubuntu host failed `[It] [sig-node] StaticPod when the static pod has init container should be ready after init container is removed and kubelet restarts`. cos host: 0 failures.

### Since when has it been failing?

Observed failing today (2026-09-16) during the weekly TestGrid review — tab was FAILING at review time with 3 consecutive failures.

### Testgrid link

https://testgrid.k8s.io/sig-node-containerd#ci-node-e2e-serial

### Reason for failure (if possible)

Truncated `failure_message` from the TestGrid summary:

```
error during go run /home/prow/go/src/k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e_node/...o/test-infra/jobs/e2e_node/containerd/image-config.yaml: exit status 1
```

This is the generic kubetest wrapper error — the real failure is the ginkgo spec failure above (different spec each run). Example tail from build `2100188711563038720/build-log.txt`:

```
command [... ginkgo --nodes=8 --skip="" --label-filter="!Flaky && Serial && NodeConformance" ...] failed with error: exit status 1
...
Step 'go run .../run_remote.go ... --image-config-file=/home/prow/go/src/k8s.io/test-infra/jobs/e2e_node/containerd/image-config.yaml' finished in 1h19m10s
...
Something went wrong: encountered 1 errors: [error during go run .../image-config.yaml: exit status 1]
```

Rotating single-spec failures across both ubuntu and cos hosts with a suite timeout in one run suggests job-level flakiness / timeout pressure rather than one broken test. Sibling job `ci-kubernetes-node-e2e-containerd-slow` shares the same wrapper signature but fails on different specs (ImageGC, MirrorPod) and started 15 days earlier (2026-09-01), so it is **not** clustered here — see #141806 discussion.

### Anything else we need to know?

- Job history: https://prow.k8s.io/job-history/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-node-e2e-containerd-serial
- Dashboard: `sig-node-containerd` only (not release-blocking).
- `linked_bugs` in TestGrid: empty.
- Related but distinct: open flake #140094 (`[Flake] kubetest.Node Tests`, same wrapper signature on sibling job `ci-kubernetes-node-e2e-containerd`, June) and open failing-test #141806 (ImageGC on the `-slow` sibling). Neither names this `-serial` job or its failing specs.
- No `kind/failing-test` + `sig/node` open issue found naming this job (searched job name, `Summary API ... PSI`, and label-filtered list).

﻿## Update: regression actually started ~2026-08-16, not 09-16 — and it's specific to this job

Dug through `finished.json`/`junit_*.xml` in the public GCS bucket back to June for this job and the sibling `ci-kubernetes-node-e2e-containerd` (#140094), no auth needed. Summary — happy to share the script/data.

### Regression started ~5 weeks before it was noticed
Weekly failure rate: Jul 5–Aug 9 sat at 8–19%. Week of **Aug 16 it jumps to 43.4%**, stays there (45%, 46%), and hits 76% by early Sep (partial week) / 47.1% over the most recent 6 days (Sep 13–18, 70 builds). A binomial changepoint scan independently pins the split at **2026-08-16 14:04 UTC** (before 14.3%, after 47.9%).

### Broad, not one flaky spec
Pre-Aug-14 vs post-Aug-17 fail counts: MirrorPod-restart 10→20, MirrorPod-volume-unmount 3→12, ImageGarbageCollect 1→8, container-lifecycle-reboot 5→8, plus new failures in GarbageCollect/Swap/PodResources/image-pull specs that barely failed before.

### Mostly timeout, not logic
78% of post-regression failed builds (59/76) have ≥1 `[TIMEDOUT]`. Failing builds average 77–79 min wall-clock vs 64–74 min for passing ones — right at ginkgo's default 70-min suite timeout (confirmed via build-log: "ginkgo flags are missing explicit --timeout... updated ginkgo flags: --timeout=70m").

### Ruled out
No k/k commit touching `pkg/kubelet`/`test/e2e_node`, no test-infra job-config or `image-config.yaml` change, and no containerd/kernel version drift (COS: containerd 2.2.6, kernel 6.12.94+ constant across 4 image respins; Ubuntu: containerd 2.1.9 constant, kernel only bumps after Aug 18 — too late) in the changepoint window.

### Sibling job (same runtime, not Serial-only) shows no spike
`ci-kubernetes-node-e2e-containerd` stays in single digits to ~20% the whole period — actually *lowest* (2.4%) the exact week this job hits 43.4%. Rules out a fleet-wide/image-wide cause; points at this job specifically, likely its all-`[Serial]` test set having far less timing margin than a parallel-eligible suite.

### Concrete mechanism, top offender
"MirrorPod when kubelet restarts should not change container status": kubelet.log shows the post-restart kubelet racing to recreate the mirror pod while the pre-restart one still exists (`already exists`), and `Ready` flaps False→True over ~254ms while it reconciles. If the node's running marginally slower, that window widens enough to trip the test's watcher more often.

### Suggested next steps
Root cause is still open (not code/config/version) — possible small general slowdown that only this job's tight timeout margin exposes. Worth: (1) bumping `--timeout` explicitly above 70m as a mitigation, (2) looping in sig-testing-infra to check GCE/Boskos latency around 2026-08-16.

/cc @harche

@harche proposed next steps, splitting this into two tracks:

1. Mitigation (this job's timeout margin)
This job runs an all-[Serial] suite with no parallel headroom, and it's now landing within a few minutes of ginkgo's 70-min default suite timeout on a regular basis. Sibling job ci-kubernetes-node-e2e-containerd (not Serial-only) shows no spike over the same period, which is consistent with this being a margin problem specific to the Serial job rather than a fleet-wide slowdown.

Proposing to open a PR against kubernetes/test-infra adding an explicit --timeout to the ginkgo flags for ci-kubernetes-node-e2e-containerd-serial (e.g. 90–100m), matching the prow job's own 90-min budget. This won't fix an underlying slowdown if there is one, but it should stop the rotating-spec noise that's currently defeating the 3-consecutive alert.

2. Root cause (why the margin got worse ~2026-08-16)
Ruled out: k/k commits touching kubelet/e2e_node, test-infra job/image-config changes, and containerd/kernel drift across the changepoint window (all constant). That points outside the repos this issue can see — GCE machine/zone behavior or Boskos project latency around us-central1-b in that window.

/cc @kubernetes/sig-testing-infra or whoever owns node-e2e Boskos capacity — did anything change around 2026-08-16 14:00 UTC in the k8s-infra-e2e-boskos-* pool or us-central1-b? Happy to share the per-build timing data if useful.

3. Separately: the MirrorPod restart race is a real, independent flake
"MirrorPod when kubelet restarts should not change container status" was already failing before Aug 16 (10 times pre-regression) and got worse after. The kubelet log shows the post-restart kubelet's first mirror-pod status write landing before its own readiness probe completes, so Ready genuinely goes False→True for a short window during every restart — not just under timeout pressure. This looks like a test assertion that's too strict for how kubelet actually reports status post-restart, independent of the timeout issue above. I'll file this as its own issue/PR once I've nailed down the exact timing, so it doesn't get lost inside this one.
@ayanasarkar If you have found the fix, please send the PR, and the review can take place there.

item.title: Add Pod and PodStatus PATCH microbenchmarks

detail.title: Add Pod and PodStatus PATCH microbenchmarks
detail.body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind cleanup
/sig api-machinery

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Adds microbenchmarks for the Pod `PATCH`, `PUT`, `POST` and `DELETE` write paths in `test/integration/apiserver/storage`, driving the apiserver handlers against a realistic Pod fixture backed by a real etcd.

The seeded Pod stores as 10,999 B of Protobuf, 11,125 B once a PATCH adds a managedFields entry. Allocation amplification against that size:

- `PATCH /pods` (`BenchmarkPatchPod`): 1,101,193 B/op (99.0x) and 16,803 allocs/op
- `PATCH /pods/status` (`BenchmarkPatchPodStatus`): 1,005,117 B/op (90.3x) and 15,414 allocs/op
- `PUT /pods` (`BenchmarkUpdatePod`): 895,941 B/op (80.5x) and 13,261 allocs/op
- `POST /pods` (`BenchmarkCreatePod`): 315,959 B/op (28.4x) and 4,124 allocs/op
- `DELETE /pods` (`BenchmarkDeletePod`): 493,911 B/op (44.4x) and 3,390 allocs/op

`BenchmarkUpdatePod` writes the same label as `BenchmarkPatchPod`, so the gap between them bounds what the strategic merge itself costs, about 19 percent of the request.

Storage is the real `etcd3.store` against the etcd process `framework.EtcdMain` already starts, via `framework.SharedEtcd()`. Because that etcd is a separate process, its bbolt and raft allocations are not counted, so `b.ReportAllocs()` still isolates the apiserver side. The counts do include the etcd clientv3 and gRPC request path, which is part of what a write costs.

Every write goes through the endpoint handlers, including the seeding, so `managedFields` are server-computed rather than supplied by the fixture. The benchmarks call `handlers.PatchResource` and friends directly rather than going through `StartTestServer`, so authn, authz and the admission chain stay out of the numbers.

```text
goos: linux
goarch: amd64
pkg: k8s.io/kubernetes/test/integration/apiserver/storage
cpu: Intel(R) Xeon(R) CPU @ 2.80GHz
BenchmarkPatchPod-32          	     300	   6711054 ns/op	 1101193 B/op	   16803 allocs/op
BenchmarkPatchPodStatus-32    	     300	   6178954 ns/op	 1005117 B/op	   15414 allocs/op
BenchmarkUpdatePod-32         	     300	   6437344 ns/op	  895941 B/op	   13261 allocs/op
BenchmarkCreatePod-32         	     300	   3607992 ns/op	  315959 B/op	    4124 allocs/op
BenchmarkDeletePod-32         	     300	   5035822 ns/op	  493911 B/op	    3390 allocs/op
```

Median of 5 runs. ns/op is fsync bound here and noisy, the allocation columns are the stable signal.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

N/A

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

Yes, AI assistance was used to draft the benchmark setup.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
NONE
```

detail.title: [Flaking Test] [sig-testing] ci-kubernetes-e2e-gce-cos-alphafeatures-master kubetest.Timeout [gce-cos-alphafeatures-master, gce-cos-alphafeatures-1.37]
detail.body:
### Which jobs are flaking?

sig-release-master-blocking#gce-cos-alphafeatures-master (`ci-kubernetes-e2e-gce-cos-alphafeatures-master`)
sig-release-1.37-blocking#gce-cos-alphafeatures-1.37 (`ci-kubernetes-e2e-gce-cos-alphafeatures-beta`, the fork of the same job)

Triage: https://storage.googleapis.com/k8s-triage/index.html?job=%5Eci-kubernetes-e2e-gce-cos-alphafeatures-master%24&test=%5ETimeout%24

Status 2026-09-22: tracked as FLAKY on the CI Signal board per the Release Signal lead. Triage accepted by SIG Node (harche); priority/critical-urgent as set at triage. I hold the Release Signal follow-up. Next step per upodroid is a test-side improvement by SIG Node; no test owner confirmed yet. The blocking or non-blocking call for v1.38.0-alpha.1 (2026-09-23) is with SIG Node and pending; no mitigation is agreed. Master count as of the 2026-09-22 16:49 UTC run is 21 of 80 (see the comments); the numbers below are the 2026-09-21 06:00 UTC snapshot.

### Which tests are flaking?

`kubetest.Timeout`. The e2e suite passes in all but one of the timed-out runs; in that one the timeout interrupted the suite.

### Since when has it been flaking?

Snapshot 2026-09-21 06:00 UTC. On master, 15 of the 61 runs since 2026-09-16 00:57 UTC hit the timeout: the first at 2026-09-17 13:04 UTC, the last two at 2026-09-21 00:16 UTC and 02:19 UTC, with passing runs in between. On the 1.37 fork, 7 of the 21 runs since 2026-09-16 01:00 UTC, the latest at 2026-09-20 13:03 UTC.

Examples:
- https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-gce-cos-alphafeatures-master/2101858636748820480 (2026-09-21 02:19 UTC)
- https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-gce-cos-alphafeatures-master/2101736329489420288 (2026-09-20 18:13 UTC)
- https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-gce-cos-alphafeatures-master/2101281830744363008 (2026-09-19 12:07 UTC)
- https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-gce-cos-alphafeatures-beta/2101658314709405696 (1.37, 2026-09-20 13:03 UTC)

### Testgrid link

https://testgrid.k8s.io/sig-release-master-blocking#gce-cos-alphafeatures-master

### Reason for failure (if possible)

The job runs out of its kubetest budget, not out of tests. It passes `--timeout=120m` to kubetest, which covers cluster up, the tests and teardown. Up and teardown are steady at about 15 minutes together, which leaves roughly 105 minutes for the suite. The suite's runtime is not fixed. The same 91 specs took 76 minutes in a passing run on 2026-09-19 at 14:08 UTC (https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-gce-cos-alphafeatures-master/2101312282582585344) and 106 minutes in the timed-out run two hours earlier (https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-gce-cos-alphafeatures-master/2101281830744363008), on the same Kubernetes commit (`v1.38.0-alpha.0.948+96b5e4e3ae3f8d`) and the same COS image. So a code or image change alone does not explain the timeouts; whether something makes the resize path slower under some conditions is open. Across the 59 runs since 2026-09-16 the test phase ranged from 76 to 113 minutes; the 45 passing runs took 76 to 103 minutes with a median of 87, and passing and timed-out runs occur on the same commits.

Almost all of that variance sits in one feature. `[Feature:InPlacePodVerticalScaling]` is 63 of the 91 specs and took 57 minutes in the fast run and 86 in the slow one; the other 28 specs took 19 minutes in both. 62 of the 63 resize specs are slower in the slow run, by 20 seconds at the median and up to 83 seconds, with no single spec standing out, so the extra time is inside the resize specs themselves. That was resolved by kubernetes/test-infra#37724: kubetest to `--timeout=180m`, the prow timeout to 3h20m, and the job moved to release-informing, on the basis that alpha-feature lanes do not fit the two-hour release-blocking budget. ### Anything else we need to know?

Update after upodroid's comment (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/142262#issuecomment-5759352510): the next step is on the test side. SIG Node is asked to look at reducing the resize specs' execution time or their run-to-run variance while keeping the coverage. Skipping the resize tests is not on the table, and a timeout increase or dashboard change is not agreed; it would come after that attempt, if at all. A test-side owner is not confirmed yet.

Background for whoever picks it up: InPlacePodVerticalScaling is Stable since 1.35, and this lane is the only blocking coverage the 63 resize specs have. ### Relevant SIG(s)

/sig testing
/sig node
/sig release

/kind flake
/priority critical-urgent
/cc @kubernetes/release-team-release-signal

/assign

Taking the Release Signal follow-up. @kubernetes/sig-node-test-failures, SIG Testing: can one of you take the technical side and say whether this blocks the alpha.1 cut on Wednesday? The evidence and the open options are in the description; nothing is agreed yet. I can open the test-infra change once there is agreement.

/triage accepted
/priority critical-urgent

Update: two more timeouts since the snapshot in the description, 2026-09-21 00:16 UTC and 02:19 UTC, both 91 Passed | 0 Failed with a 107-minute test phase on v1.38.0-alpha.0.950. Edited 2026-09-21: the paragraph below replaces one that used only this job's own runs, which are cut off at the timeout. Since 09-10: 135 runs, max 116. Its wall time p75 is 125 minutes, over the 120-minute p75 target in release-blocking-jobs.md. With about 15 minutes of non-test steps, a 130m kubetest budget would have left roughly 2 to 6% of those runs timing out and 135m roughly 0 to 1%; 135m leaves only the 15-minute interrupt grace between kubetest and the 2h30m prow cap that the blocking policy test enforces. None of this is agreed; it is here so the owners can choose.

> * Trimming InPlacePodVerticalScaling out of the focus would cut about three-quarters of the runtime

We can't skip testing features. SIG Node needs to modify that test so it runs faster.

Can SIG Node reengineer this test to reduce execution time or reduce variance in test duration? I would like to see this attempted first before we discuss increasing the test timeout.

btw, this situation will only get worse as we add more features

I pulled `artifacts/ginkgo/report.json` for the two runs in the description (same commit, 63 resize specs, 57 vs 86 minutes) and split each spec by its `By` steps and the klog lines it captured.

Most of the time is exec. Each run does 1104 execs into the test pod to read cgroup files (547 `head -n 1 cpu.weight`, 243 `memory.max`, 243 `cpu.max`, 70 `cat /proc/1/oom_score_adj`, 1 `mount -t cgroup2`), 3 to 30 per spec, and 61 of the 63 specs issue the exact same sequence in both runs. The fixtures use 25m to 35m limits, so the shell that exec starts gets 2.5 to 3.5 ms per 100 ms. That fits the numbers. How badly it throttles would depend on the host, which would explain the day-to-day swing. I cannot tell from the logs why Guaranteed pods come out slower than Burstable pods with the same limits. The 1.37 fork has the older helper but the same exec checks.

So in these two runs the resize wait did not get slower; the exec-based cgroup checks did. Throttling fits the timings. The timings alone do not prove it. Reading the values without an exec in the throttled container, or at least doing one exec for the three files instead of three, should remove most of that time while keeping the same checks. If SIG Node wants the batching tried I can send a PR.

> > * Trimming InPlacePodVerticalScaling out of the focus would cut about three-quarters of the runtime
> 
> We can't skip testing features. SIG Node needs to modify that test so it runs faster.
> 
> Can SIG Node reengineer this test to reduce execution time or reduce variance in test duration? I would like to see this attempted first before we discuss increasing the test timeout.
> 
> btw, this situation will only get worse as we add more features

For sig-node we have been moving some of these tests to a slow lane

Reproduced the exec cost outside CI with podman (runc 1.4.0) on a desktop i5-14500: a `busybox:1.36` container idling in `sh -c 'trap exit TERM; while true; do sleep 1; done'`, then timing `podman exec ctr /bin/sh -c 'head -n 1 /sys/fs/cgroup/cpu.max'`, 6 to 8 runs per point, medians.

No CPU limit 0.20 s; `--cpus 0.025`: 2.6 to 2.8 s; 0.03: 2.3 to 3.0 s; 0.035: 1.7 to 2.0 s; 0.05: 1.7 s; 0.1: 0.6 s; 0.2: 0.3 s; 0.3 and 1.0: 0.2 s. The ranges are two sessions; within a session the order is monotonic.

So a container limited to 25m to 35m costs about 2 to 3 s per exec even on a fast CPU; the e2e nodes are e2-standard-2. Most of that is the exec setup inside the throttled cgroup, not the shell. In the same 30m container, interleaved: `sh -c head` 2.5 s, `head` with no shell 2.5 s, `cat` 2.2 s, and one `sh -c head` reading all three files 2.2 s. On the test side that leaves, smallest change first: raise the fixture limits (an exec is 0.6 s at 100m and 0.3 s at 200m), read the three files in one exec per check, or read them without exec.

`TearDown` follow-up for the two runs Jubitta reported in the Release Signal Slack thread:

- https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-gce-cos-alphafeatures-master/2102165921954009088
- https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-gce-cos-alphafeatures-master/2102318176564940800

Both are the tracked pattern: the suite passes, then the kubetest timer interrupts `e2e-down.sh`.

| Build | Run start, UTC | Suite | `Test` | `TearDown` | `Deferred TearDown` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2102165921954009088 | 2026-09-21 22:40 | 91 Passed, 0 Failed | 106.1 min | Started at minute 115 of the 120 min budget. Interrupted 4m52s later, after the subnet was already deleted. | Completed in 55s |
| 2102318176564940800 | 2026-09-22 08:45 | 91 Passed, 0 Failed | 107.4 min | Started at minute 117. Interrupted 2m35s later, while `kube-down` was still working on the instance group and the master. | Completed in 2m31s |

I found no cleanup error before the interrupt in either build log. In five other reviewed runs the `TearDown` step completed in 5.2 to 5.5 minutes, so these two were cut short, not slow.

The `Error: 58 leaked resources` line in 2102318176564940800 comes from the resource listing that runs between the interrupted `TearDown` and the deferred one. It lists what was still there at that moment. There is no listing after the deferred run, so I cannot say what remained.

I am keeping these two here. No separate issue.

Master count, same window as the description (2026-09-16 00:57 UTC through the 2026-09-22 16:49 UTC run, which also timed out): 21 of 80 completed runs hit `kubetest.Timeout`, about 26%. 20 of the 21 finished the suite; one was interrupted mid-suite. The two runs above are in that count.

That covers the tracking question. The test-time problem and the alpha.1 call are still open.

item.title: Test coverage of volume relabeling is lacking

detail.title: Test coverage of volume relabeling is lacking
detail.body:
**What happened**:
SELinux volume relabeling regressed in 1.16/1.17 with no test failures. See https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/83679

**What you expected to happen**:
Test failures would have prevented the regression. Currently, we apparently only have manual test guarantees that this functions correctly.

/sig node storage
/priority critical-urgent

comments.body:
in the place where we are running this test, it appears to be failing 100% of the time:

https://testgrid.k8s.io/google-gce#gci-gce-flaky&sort-by-flakiness=&width=20&include-filter-by-regex=SELinux
/assign @gnufied

@gnufied https://testgrid.k8s.io/google-gce#gci-gce-flaky&sort-by-flakiness=&width=20&include-filter-by-regex=SELinux looks solidly green now, can the `[Flaky]` tag be removed to ensure test coverage now?

@liggitt flaky can definitely be removed from these tests, but looking at the logs:

```
 543   │ I0312 00:28:29.269] Mar 12 00:28:29.269: INFO: Running '/workspace/kubernetes/platforms/linux/amd64/kubectl exec --namespace=securit
       │ y-context-9753 security-context-21e88fa6-71c5-4175-8aa4-96bfe0289fce -c=test-container -- cat /sys/fs/selinux/enforce'
 544   │ I0312 00:28:29.918] Mar 12 00:28:29.917: INFO: error running kubectl exec to read file: exit status 1
 545   │ I0312 00:28:29.918] stdout=
 546   │ I0312 00:28:29.918] stderr=cat: can't open '/sys/fs/selinux/enforce': No such file or directory
 547   │ I0312 00:28:29.918] command terminated with exit code 1
 548   │ I0312 00:28:29.918] )

```

They are just skipping the bits that depend on selinux and hence is green. Do we have different configuration where selinux is enabled?
… so we still don't actually have coverage of the feature anywhere that would be visible to the release team?

Storage team has enough coverage for their features (SELinuxMount & related feature gates). We don't feel responsible for testing of relabeling done by the container runtime(s) ;-).

It is trivial to add a test that needs SELinux, just mark it with `[Feature:SELinux]` and it will run in CI jobs [kops-aws-selinux](https://testgrid.k8s.io/kops-k8s-ci#kops-aws-selinux) and `pull-kubernetes-e2e-gce-storage-selinux`. item.title: sig-node: exclude [Slow] specs from ci-kubernetes-node-e2e-containerd-serial

detail.title: sig-node: exclude [Slow] specs from ci-kubernetes-node-e2e-containerd-serial
detail.body:
﻿## What this does
Excludes `[Slow]` specs from `ci-kubernetes-node-e2e-containerd-serial` by adding `!Slow` to the ginkgo label filter (`!Flaky && !Slow && Serial && NodeConformance`), instead of the timeout bump originally proposed.

## Why
kubernetes/kubernetes#142147 tracks this job intermittently failing with `[TIMEDOUT]` across rotating, unrelated specs since ~2026-08-16. Investigation found the job's Serial suite was landing right at its ~70m implicit ginkgo timeout on affected runs.

Per @harche's review: the `[Slow]` specs in this job's Serial+NodeConformance set — mainly MirrorPod and ImageGC — cost ~30m/host and already run in `ci-kubernetes-node-e2e-containerd-slow`, whose filter (`!Flaky && Slow && NodeConformance`) has no `Serial` exclusion. So these specs were running redundantly in both jobs, not exclusively here. Confirmed via direct inspection of `-slow`'s config — no coverage gap from removing them (see PR comment below).

Root cause of the underlying slowdown is still open on the linked issue — image pre-pull time doubling fleet-wide since ~08-12 is the current leading theory, being discussed separately with sig-testing-infra. This PR only removes the duplicated `[Slow]` execution; no timeout values are changed.

Ref: kubernetes/kubernetes#142147

Instead of bumping timeouts, can we add `!Slow` to the label filter (`!Flaky && !Slow && Serial && NodeConformance`)? The ImageGC and MirrorPod `[Slow]` specs account for about 30 min per host and already run in `ci-kubernetes-node-e2e-containerd-slow`, and the real slowdown is image pre-pull, which doubled across all node e2e jobs starting 08-12, not just this one.
/cc @kannon92
/ok-to-test

@harche Confirmed no coverage gap: ci-kubernetes-node-e2e-containerd-slow's filter is '!Flaky && Slow && NodeConformance' with no Serial exclusion, so it already runs the Serial+Slow+NodeConformance specs (MirrorPod, ImageGC) today. They were running redundantly in both jobs before this change, not exclusively in -serial. This PR just removes the duplication.

> The ImageGC and MirrorPod `[Slow]` specs account for about 30 min per host

This doesn't make sense and needs to be fixed. These are VMs running in the cloud, and image downloads shouldn't take that long.

What images are we pulling? How big are they? Can we use newer images that are leaner?

> > The ImageGC and MirrorPod `[Slow]` specs account for about 30 min per host
> 
> This doesn't make sense and needs to be fixed. These are VMs running in the cloud, and image downloads shouldn't take that long.
> 
> What images are we pulling? How big are they? Can we use newer images that are leaner?

@upodroid thanks for pushing on this fair question and worth actually checking rather than assuming. i dug into the test source to see whats really driving the time.

turns out it's not image size or pull time

the images involved are the standard e2e-test-images set — pause, busybox, nginx-slim/agnhost — a few MB each, the same images used across most of the e2e_node suite. So they don't seem like a likely bottleneck on their own.
The ~30m looks like it comes from wait/poll budgets built into the tests themselves:
image_gc_test.go: the two [Slow] specs each poll for up to checkGCUntil = 6 * time.Minute. The code comment explains why — they're bound by the kubelet's ImageGCPeriod, which is hardcoded to 5 minutes.
garbage_collector_test.go: setupDuration = 10 * time.Minute, garbageCollectDuration = 3 * time.Minute.
mirror_pod_test.go: a lot of 2*time.Minute Eventually polls spread across its specs, plus a couple of 5*time.Minute waits.

So it looks like leaner images wouldn't move the needle much here — the time is baked into how these specs wait on a hardcoded kubelet GC interval. I've updated the PR description to reflect this instead of the "images are big" framing, since that wasn't quite right and I don't want to leave a misleading rationale in there.

If it's useful, I'm happy to open a follow-up looking at whether ImageGCPeriod could be made configurable for tests, so specs like this don't have to wait on the production default — but that felt out of scope for this PR, which is just about removing the duplicated execution between -serial and -slow. Let me know if you'd rather I hold off on merging this one until that's discussed.
Can we poll more frequently? If the test was written a long time, it's probably worth revisiting it's approach and assumptions.

> Can we poll more frequently? If the test was written a long time, it's probably worth revisiting it's approach and assumptions.

good thoughtbut tightening the poll interval won't help here these tests aren't slow because they check too infrequently, they're slow because they're waiting on a real event (kubelet GC) that's gated by ImageGCPeriod, hardcoded to 5 min. Polling faster just means more no-op checks while we wait for the same 5-6 min window to pass.

youre right that it's worth revisiting though i think the real fix is making ImageGCPeriod configurable for tests, so we're not bound to the production default. happy to open a follow-up issue for thatseparate from this PR.
